hero.title: The law changes every year. Konta updates itself, with no contractor and no fee.
hero.lead: An accounting platform for companies and accounting firms in the Republic of Moldova. Fiscal rules are versioned data, published in the open, rather than code written separately for every installation. Built on the SNC, the Fiscal Code and e-Factura.
set.title: Fiscal rule set 2026
set.note: The set is being checked by a licensed accountant and is not yet approved for production. Until it is, you can read and verify it yourself, one value at a time.
ef.title: The e-Factura mandate
ef.p1: Business-to-business electronic invoicing is scheduled to become mandatory on 1 October 2026, and a paper invoice loses its value for deducting VAT. If you are changing how you issue invoices anyway, this is the cheapest moment it will ever be.
ef.p2: Konta handles e-Factura for every client company from one screen, and purchase invoices that arrive as XML are posted automatically. The sales and purchase registers fill from what already went through SFS, not from what you re-typed.
ef.p3: The VAT refund ceiling was raised to 70% for taxpayers using e-Factura or MEV. That is a cash-flow gain you can calculate for each client individually.
ef.caveat: The 1 October 2026 date is reported by international VAT trackers. We are confirming it against the Moldovan legal act before treating it as settled, and will publish the answer here.
law.title: Why data, and not code
law.p1: Where the rules are programmed, every change in the law is a paid contractor visit, separately for each installation. The 2027 fiscal reform has already passed its first reading. Here is what it contains.
law.c1: New registration of Individual Enterprises and Peasant Farms closes
law.c2: Peasant farm income tax rises from 7% to 12%
law.c3: Dividend tax rises from 6% to 8% on profit earned after 2027
law.c4: The preferential small-trader rate rises from 1% to 3% of revenue
law.c5: CAEM revision 2.1 re-codes the activity classification of every entity
law.p2: For us, every row above is one new record in the rulebook, published to all customers on the same day and verifiable by anyone. Not a recompiled version, installation by installation, for a fee.
price.title: Price
price.p1: Published, in lei, per month. No implementation fee, and no charge for legislative updates, ever.
price.w1: One non-VAT micro-entity, under roughly 50 documents a month
price.w3: Small company, with payroll, inventory and several users
price.w4: Medium company, multiple entities, API, production
price.w5: Accounting firms, per client company, tiered by volume
price.note: Indicative prices. We confirm them before launch, and once published they do not rise for an existing customer because the law changed.
move.title: Moving off 1C
move.p1: Send us the database copy on Monday, work in Konta on Wednesday. We migrate the first company of any accounting firm ourselves, free; the second one you will do yourselves in a few hours.
move.p2: We run in parallel for as long as you need, so the switch rests on reconciled figures rather than on trust. The numpad keys you use in 1C stay the same, and the interface is Romanian and Russian at parity, not half translated.
open.title: Transparency
open.p1: We are asking you to trust us with payroll and with your clients' books. Here is what you can check yourself, without asking us.
open.b1: Anyone can read which rate we apply, from which date, and on the authority of which act. If a figure is wrong, it is visible from outside.
open.b2: The code that talks to SFS on your behalf can be read by anyone, line by line.
open.b3: Your data comes out in open formats, at any time, with no request and no fee. Leaving us should be as easy as joining.
open.b4: This page carries no analytics and no trackers. No request from your browser goes anywhere but konta.md, the fonts included.
contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: A person answers, in Romanian or Russian. If you are an accounting firm and the e-Factura mandate is on your mind, call; the conversation takes a quarter of an hour.
